cases.task: Revise an earlier mega-base idea after learning that the save is still on a level-0 Base Core and only Update 1 content may be used. Produce a durable factory checkpoint with the revised architecture, live logistics choices, buffers and exports, one defense provision, and the open in-game questions that should be tested next.

answer.answer: PVE34 proved that the 10M crossing was clean and write-path-limited, but the later autonomy work superseded PVE34 as an operating identity: worker counts became reversible, scenario-specific control variables. The next safe experiment is a bounded longer alpha soak with host pressure observed, preceded by hard-kill/restart recovery proof and the full integrity gate set.

claims.value: The historical 10M Nyx checkpoint was `split-lanes-64f-pve34-pvp2-other1-200k-to10m-20260523T115711Z`: it inserted `210624` rows, finished at `10.019M`, crossed `10,000,000` at elapsed `442s`, averaged about `403/sec` during elapsed `220-490s`, and recorded `0` parser errors, retries, duplicates, or terminal markers. Summary recompute for `1-10019225`, sampled membership, S3, coverage-window, and protected-D2-Redis validation passed. It established PVE34 as the best practical profile for that Nyx data band and showed the write path—not fetch—was limiting, with substantial idle headroom; the preceding 250k keeper run reached about `447/sec` steady and validated cleanly with membership sharding off.

The durable autonomy evidence superseded fixed PVE34-style tuning as the operating model: worker counts are evidence, not identity, and fetch, feeder, batch, DB/write lanes, and rollup/S3 workers should adapt through cooldowns, rollback, bad-trial memory, queue pressure, and host pressure. Later verified scenarios showed alpha above `1k/sec` (best current-code average `1083.1 PGCR/sec`), beta scaling fetch to `128` under `760ms` latency, delta reducing fetch/retry to floor `4`, and gamma parser-owned S3 averaging `2141.3/sec` while shifting the bottleneck toward DB/write lanes. Consequently `112`, PVE34, and `36/5` are not universal defaults: alpha often rejects `35/6 -> 36/5`, while gamma may accept it under S3 abundance.

claims.value: The non-negotiable model is that data integrity beats throughput, DB rows are truth, raw marker commits travel with summaries, autoscaler state is optimization state rather than correctness state, and normal parser restart from DB truth is the only recovery mechanism. There must be no D1 rebuild/recompute path, parser-state correctness table, or Cortex S3 replay into DB writes; parser-owned S3 reads remain in the parser fetch path, and protected D2 Redis namespaces remain read-only. Required gates include `dev/scripts/d1-milestone-status.sh`, unchanged protected D2 Redis counts, contiguous raw coverage by count, `raw_failed_pgcrs=0`, S3 ledger/readback verification, a cache tail containing only the normal partial batch, Datadog visibility, healthy host Redis, acceptable MySQL/host memory and CPU pressure, and no active parser/Cortex process after bounded runs. A hard-kill/restart recovery proof is mandatory before an unattended long run; DB unavailability must stop the parser rather than spin, and failed rows retry immediately at startup.
source_paths: Projects/Warmind/D1 parser autonomy and autotuning context summary - 2026-05-25.md

claims.value: The next safe performance experiment is a bounded longer alpha soak using learned priors, with MySQL/host memory and CPU pressure included in the decision loop and DB rebalancing limited initially to reversible, fixed-budget one-worker moves. Before extending it into an unattended run, first prove hard-kill/restart recovery from DB truth and pass every integrity gate: milestone status, protected D2 Redis counts, contiguous coverage, `raw_failed_pgcrs=0`, S3 ledger/readback, partial-batch-only cache tail, Datadog and Redis health, host/MySQL pressure checks, and confirmation that no parser/Cortex process survives the bounded run. Beta latency-removal recovery, delta cadence, gamma DB lanes, and active rollup-worker autotuning remain separate incomplete follow-up work.

decisions: Do not treat PVE34, fetch `112`, or DB split `36/5` as universal defaults.
Keep trials reversible and scenario-specific, with integrity gates ahead of throughput.
Require hard-kill/restart proof before any unattended long run.

Does beta reliably reduce high fetch after artificial latency is removed?
What delta cadence and slow-edge fetch/batch policy should be used?
Should rollup worker count become actively autotuned?

Run the recovery proof and complete integrity gates.

Package incomplete autonomy work into small reviewable commits after verification.

answer.answer: The mega-base is superseded by a distributed, level-0-safe Update 1 plan. The architecture is a proposal; no completed in-game build or measured throughput is established. Durable checkpoint saved as checkpoint:3df859b1-912e-98b0-6a5e-e4be4b55aace.

claims.value: Revised architecture: while the save remains on the level-0 Base Core, keep powered-building heat at or below its 1,000 capacity because exceeding capacity disables Fire Wave protection. Replace the earlier mega-base with distributed mining outposts connected to a compact Base Core production district by rail trunks that carry both power and materials. Use v.2/v.3 trunks only for aggregated traffic, Junctions or Roundabouts at district boundaries, and spurs sized to individual flows. This is a proposed architecture, not a verified in-game implementation. Use only Update 1 content: Rail v.1/v.2/v.3 are available, while v.4/v.5 are future content. Do not co-locate a 500-heat Constructorizer and 650-heat Facturer under the current core because their combined 1,150 heat already exceeds its capacity.

Live logistics and buffering choice for the revised plan: use one item per line where possible and match rail capacity to actual source rate—Rail v.1 carries 120 items/min, v.2 carries 240 items/min, and v.3 carries 480 items/min. A v.1 Ore Excavator produces 120/min on Normal and 240/min on Pure; a v.2 Excavator produces 300/min on Normal and 480/min on Pure; Helium-3 and Sulfur Extractors each produce 240/min. Upgrade only aggregated trunks rather than every line. Put a single-item Storage Depot v.1 with capacity 400 or v.2 with capacity 1,600 on each production line. When available and affordable, place the 2,500-capacity multi-item Multistorage at the end of the bus as an overflow sink so backed-up destinations do not halt producers. These are selected operating rules, but sustained in-game flow has not yet been verified.

Exports and defense: dedicate one Orbital Cargo Launcher per export product because each launcher has one input; feed every launcher from its own buffer depot so corporation-reputation exports do not starve. Actual export products must be chosen from the save’s current corporation goals, since the evidence does not establish them. For defense, run a thin Rail v.1 ammo loop from the ammo printer to Defense Towers, which can be resupplied by drone rail; Defense Turret t1 remains manual-feed only. Keep this provision within the same 1,000-capacity level-0 heat ceiling so Fire Wave protection remains active.

Open in-game verification questions: (1) Do drones use round-robin or priority queueing at Rail Modulator merges? (2) Do Multirail lanes share throughput or behave as independent rails? (3) What is the Drone Station coverage radius? (4) Is Delivery Storage available in Update 1? (5) What capacity do Base Core Amplifier v.1 and v.2 actually add, since their +50/+20 descriptions conflict with temperature fields of −250 and −20? (6) Does the in-game Base Core upgrade item mix match the source data? Also measure one representative source-to-buffer line against its expected 120/240/480 items/min rail breakpoint before scaling the architecture.

checkpoint.objective: Revise the earlier Star Rupture mega-base into a durable Update 1 factory plan that remains safe on the current level-0 Base Core.
current_state: Verified: the level-0 Base Core has 1,000 capacity, and exceeding it disables Fire Wave protection.
Verified: Update 1 rails v.1/v.2/v.3 carry 120/240/480 items per minute and conduct electricity; v.4/v.5 are not yet in game.
Proposed, not implemented or measured: distributed mining outposts connected to a compact production district by rate-matched powered rail trunks and spurs.
No completed in-game factory state or live throughput result is established by the evidence.
decisions: Keep powered-building heat at or below 1,000 until the Base Core is upgraded.
Use distributed outposts, backbone-plus-spur routing, and upgrades only on aggregated trunks.
Prefer one item per line with 400- or 1,600-capacity buffers; reserve 2,500-capacity Multistorage for end-of-bus overflow.
Use one buffered Orbital Cargo Launcher per chosen export product.
Supply Defense Towers through a Rail v.1 ammo loop; manually feed Defense Turret t1.
open_questions: Rail Modulator merge ordering: round-robin or priority?
Whether Multirail lanes share throughput or operate independently.
Actual amplifier capacity values given the source discrepancy.
Whether Base Core upgrade item mixes match the current game.
next_actions: Inventory all powered buildings and total their heat before expanding; remain at or below 1,000.
Build and measure one representative source-to-buffer spur against its expected rail-tier throughput.
Test merge ordering, Multirail behavior, Drone Station reach, and Delivery Storage availability.
Verify amplifier effects and Base Core upgrade costs in the current save.
Select export products from current corporation goals and assign each a buffered launcher.
